headline: FAA declares rare, widespread ground outage

paragraphs.text: Nearly 8,000 flights are delayed so far
Jets on the tarmac at LaGuardia Airport.
The Federal Aviation Administration declared a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday, citing a "communication issue" impacting traffic control centers.
According to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, FAA technicians are investigating the issue.
Nearly 8,000 flights within, into, or out of the U.S. are delayed on Friday, according to FlightAware. Total cancellations for the day hit 930 flights.
Most affected airports included New York's JFK airport as well as Boston's Logan and San Francisco's airports.
"This has been in the making for the last 20 years, in terms of air traffic-control modernization," said Ernie Arvai, president of AirInsight Group.
"We have talked about it forever, and not done much about it," he said. "I feel bad for all the people today who are going to be stuck."

The last time there was a nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, after a failure of a pilot-alert system. Before that, the last such nationwide stop was after the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.
